# **Side navigation**

| ![][image1] | The side navigation component provides users with a way to navigate through various sections, features, or pages of an application. It appears as a vertical panel on the left side of the screen. The navigation can have two levels:  The primary and the secondary navigation.  The primary navigation is always shown.  The secondary navigation can be used as needed to display a second level of navigation. Figma component: [Figma](https://www.figma.com/design/KHJBlNJnoTEoLXzwjWSI9l/%E2%98%A0%EF%B8%8F-%5BWIP---DO-NOT-USE%5D-Applications---Core-component-library?node-id=0-1&t=qdWe0W3ougtiXe6b-1) Last modified: 29 Jul 2024 Spec status: Spec Done  Component status: Req. & Benchmarking Done UX Design Done Visual Done Implementation In-progress User research Blocked   |
| ----: | :---- |

# **Anatomy**

## Primary navigation (expanded)

The expanded primary navigation has 3 sections:

1. Navigation header  
2. Navigation content  
3. Navigation footer

The navigation header and the navigation footer (and their sub-components) are the predefined parts of the navigation. The navigation content has one mandatory item, a collapsible navigation item titled “Help” which at the very least must include an [external link](https://ubuntu.com/legal) to our legal information.  
Apart from that the content of the navigation is defined by the designer and may contain the following elements and sub-components:

* Group header  
* context switcher  
* Navigation item  
* Separator

![][image2]

## Primary navigation (collapsed)

The collapsed primary navigation has 3 sections:

1. Logo  
2. Expand button  
3. Navigation footer

![][image3]

## Secondary navigation

The secondary navigation has 2 sections:

1. Navigation header  
2. Navigation content

The navigation header is the predefined part of the secondary navigation.  
The content of the navigation is defined by the designer and may contain the following elements and sub-components:

* Group header  
* Navigation item

![][image4]

## Sub-components

### Navigation item

![][image5]

### Context switcher

The context switcher is a drop down. It includes the drop down field, the context list and a “create   
context button. 

![][image6]

# **Usage**

## Primary navigation (expanded)

The primary navigation is displayed at all times in a Canonical application, apart from if a user is not logged in. 

#### Header

* The header is displayed at all times  
* The expand/collapse functionality of the primary navigation cannot be disabled. 

#### Content

The Navigation content is defined by the designer and can include the following sub-components:

* Context switcher  
* Navigation item  
* Separator  
* Group header

The designer can use and arrange the sub-components in this section as they see fit. The primary navigation can be split into groups. Inside a group, all items should either have or not have an icon, these should not be mixed. These groups can have an optional group header. 

#### Footer

The footer is reserved for user-related content, and may contain account settings, notifications and logout. All footer items are optional.  
If the application allows for a certificate user (like LXD) then instead of the profile icon the certificate icon is used and the logout option is hidden.  
 

## Primary navigation (collapsed)

#### Navigation items

The collapsed state of the side navigation will not show navigation items for the following reasons:

* In order to theoretically show navigation items in the collapsed state they need to have an icon. We can not guarantee that every navigation item will have an icon. If it didn’t have an icon the navigation items would either jump around on expand/collapse or have big whitespaces between them.  
* Navigation items which have a context switcher would not be able to show it properly in the collapsed state \- again making navigation items jump.  
* There is undefined behaviour for navigation which have expandable/collapsible navigation items. What would happen to an expanded navigation item when the navigation collapses? Does it collapse the navigation item (makes navigation items jump) or stay open (big whitespace).  
* The expand button needs to move down in the collapsed state \- making navigation items jump.  
* It is not good UX practice to have Icon buttons without labels, especially for more ambiguous/abstract icons like we sometimes have in our navigation items. The collapsed state would not be able to properly show labels for navigation items.

## Secondary navigation

The secondary navigation can be used as a second level of navigation as designers see fit. The suggested usage for a secondary navigation is if there are a lot (5+) second level navigation items which would be too many to fit inside a collapsible navigation item. A common use case would be settings, for example.

#### Title

Reflects the name of the expanded primary navigation item. Sometimes this is not the case; for example, when there is an item in the primary navigation named after the user’s username, and it expands a secondary navigation with the title “Account settings”. In this case, the title reflects the nature of the items of the navigation, and not the original label. 

#### Content

The Navigation content is defined by the designer and can include the following sub-components:

* Group header  
* Navigation item

In the secondary navigation, the designer can include only navigation items that are not expandable and without icons. These items can be grouped under headers and a separator can be used to separate different sections of the content. 

## Sub-components

### Navigation item

Navigation items constitute the side navigation.

#### Icons

Icons are used to graphically represent the meaning of the item text. They are optional, as not every concept can be represented with an icon. Items with or without icons should not be mixed inside the same section of the navigation. 

#### Grouping

A header can be used to group navigation items. Group titles describe the category that the items in the group belong to. Grouping divides the navigation into different categories of items. 

#### Expandable

Navigation items can have children. The expandable item itself can not link to any page. The only click interaction an expandable item can have is expanding/collapsing its children. Use the children to link to pages in your application. Children should be grouped either inside an expandable item or displayed inside the secondary navigation. If an item has more than 5 children, it is preferable to use the secondary navigation.

Take into account that children of an expandable item aren’t always being displayed, so the parent item should have a name that allows the user to discover them. 

#### Badge

Badges are used within navigation items to convey dynamic information related to that item, for example notifications that require an action or highlight a change. 

### Context switcher

Use the context switcher if your product classifies parts of your product into different contexts, projects, users, or similar. In this case, the pages of your product’s navigation would be the same for every context, but the content would vary depending on the context. 

#### Context switcher item

The items in the content switcher are user-generated. The user should be able to create new contexts and they will be listed inside the dropdown. 

A content switcher item can have a badge, which should be used to convey dynamic and actionable information related to that context. Badges indicate a quantifiable status change. They shouldn’t be used to convey passive information.

# **Interactions**

## Primary navigation (expanded)

#### Logo

**Hover**  
The default cursor will change to a pointer cursor to indicate that the item is clickable. 

##### Click

On-click the user is forwarded to the page specified in the logo-target property (which by default is the first item of the navigation that is a page). The designer can change the target by changing the page specified in the logo-target property. We recommend using a page which offers the most general view of the application, or the most used section.  
	

#### Collapse/expand button

**Hover**

|  ![][image7] | When the mouse pointer hovers over the button, the background colour of the collapse/expand button changes and the cursor changes to cursor-pointer. If the mouse pointer hovers over the collapse/expand button for 1 second, a tooltip is displayed on the right and in the centre of the button saying either "Collapse" or "Expand" depending on the status of the navigation. The transition is not animated |
| :---- | :---- |

##### Click

If the collapse/expand button is clicked it inverts the [is-open](#is-open) state of the primary navigation to either expand or collapse the navigation. On-click the background colour of the button changes.

##### Keyboard shortcut

When the user hits "ctrl \+ E", the side navigation toggles between expanded and collapsed states by reversing the is-open status. Single-letter shortcuts like "A" are preferred in web applications because many command/shift combinations are already reserved by the operating system or browser. The letter "A" is particularly convenient since it's on the left side of the keyboard, close to where the user's hand often rests, and aligns with the side navigation's location.

#### Footer

**Hover**  
See navigation item interactions.

##### Click

If the account navigation item of the footer is clicked the account settings page of the application is opened. If the notifications navigation item of the footer is clicked the notification page of the application is opened. If the log out navigation item of the footer is clicked the user is logged out from the application.

## Primary navigation (collapsed)

#### Footer

|  ![][image8] | In the collapsed state the footer items show their labels in tooltips when hovered after a 800ms delay. |
| :---- | :---- |

## Secondary navigation

The designer can define an item of the primary navigation to display its children in a secondary navigation. If a user clicks on such items, the secondary navigation will be displayed. 

The secondary navigation cannot be collapsed. 

It is hidden as soon as a user clicks on an element of the primary navigation that does not display its children in a secondary navigation.

## Sub-components

### Navigation item

##### Hover

On-Hover the background colour of the navigation item changes and the cursor changes to cursor-pointer.

##### Click

| ![][image9] | If the navigation item is expandable, on clicking the item, the state of the navigation item will change to expanded or collapsed depending on its previous state. The chevron is rotated to the open or closed position. The transition is animated as shown in the example. |
| :---- | :---- |

If it's a normal navigation item, on click, the user is forwarded to the page specified in the target of the navigation item.

### Context switcher

##### Hover

On hover, the background colour of the context switcher dropdown, the context switcher item and the create context button changes and the cursor changes to cursor-pointer.

##### Click

If the context switcher dropdown is clicked, the is-open property of the context switcher is inverted to either show or hide the context list.

If a context switcher item is clicked, the current context is set to the context which was clicked on. This will potentially refresh the content of the page, to reflect the newly selected context. Alternatively, the user will be forwarded to the page of the newly selected context.

If the create context button is clicked the user is forwarded to the page where a new context can be created.

# **Responsive**

The height of the navigation is 100% of the viewport and the width of the navigation is 240px on all breakpoints above the small breakpoint of Vanilla. At breakpoints below small, a customised version of the side navigation is used that is optimised for mobile use and described in the following section.

| ![][image10] | The collapse expand button is replaced by a button which reads “Menu”. On mobile the header is always shown, while the body is hidden. If the menu button in the header is clicked the content and footer of the navigation is shown. |
| :---- | :---- |

| ![][image11] | The menu opens to be full screen. The menu button text changes to “Close menu”. The styling of the navigation stays the same for the most part. Same whitespace, gradients, sticky footer etc. |
| :---- | :---- |

##### Context switcher

| ![][image12] | The context switcher will appear in the same position of the navigation as on desktop. When a user opens the dropdown, the context list will be displayed on top of the content of the navigation. When the context is switched, the navigation will close and the same page will be displayed for the new context selected. If the previous page wasn’t part of the context group, the default page of the context will be opened. |
| :---- | :---- |

##### Items with children and secondary navigation

| ![][image13] | When an item has children, this will be signalled with a chevron pointing to the right. When a user clicks on this item, its children will be displayed in a new page of the navigation.  This is the same behaviour as for example navigation on sites like ubuntu.com. Both expandable items and items that open in a secondary navigation will behave in the same way on mobile. If the user clicks on such an expandable item / secondary nav item, there will be a back button displayed at the top of the navigation with a chevron pointing to the left. |
| :---- | :---- |

# **Properties**

### Primary navigation

#### logo

With the logo property the product logo which is to be displayed at the top of the primary navigation can be chosen.

##### Type

Single select

##### Options

* Anbox  
* JAAS  
* Kernel Factory  
* LXD  
* Landscape  
* MAAS  
* Multipass  
* Site Manager

#### logo-target

The logo-target property specifies the target page to which the user is forwarded to when clicking on the logo.

##### Type

URL

##### Constraints

External URLs are not allowed, only URLs that forward to pages of the application itself.

##### Options

The default target is the page of the first navigation item in the primary navigation.

---

#### is-open {#is-open}

With the is-open property the primary navigation can be opened or closed.

##### Type

Boolean

##### Options

The is-open property has the following options:

* true (default)  
* false

#### footer-items

With the footer-items property the items which should be shown in the footer of the primary navigation can be chosen. If none is selected the footer is hidden.

##### Type

Multi select

##### Options

* Account (settings)  
* Notification  
* Log out

---

#### content

With the content property the navigation content (2) can be set.

##### Type

Salad bar

##### Constraint

Only the following Elements/Sub-components can be given as children in the content property:

* Group header  
* context switcher  
* Navigation item  
* Separator

### Secondary navigation

#### title

With the title property the title that is to be displayed at the top of the secondary navigation can be set.

##### Type

Text

---

#### content

With the content property the navigation content (2) can be set.

##### Type

Children

##### Constraint

Only the following Elements/Sub-components can be given as children in the content property:

* Group header  
* Navigation item

### Sub–components

#### Navigation item

##### target

Where the user is forwarded to when they click on the navigation item.

###### *Type*

URL

###### *Constraints*

If the expandable property is true a target can not be set.

---

##### icon

With the icon property the icon that is displayed at the start of the navigation item can be chosen.

###### *Type*

Single select

###### *Options*

All icons that are available in Vanilla can be chosen.

---

##### show-icon

With the show-icon property the icon can be shown or hidden

###### *Type*

Boolean

###### *Options*

* true (default)  
* false

###### *Constraint*

If indented is false show-icon must also be false

---

##### indented

With the indented property it can be chosen whether item-text should be indented or not.

###### *Type*

Boolean

###### *Options*

* true (default)  
* False

###### *Constraints*

It must be indented if an icon is used. (Indented can not be false if show-icon is true.)

##### item-text

With the item-text property the navigation items text can be set.

###### *Type*

Text

---

##### badge

With the badge property the badge of the navigation item can be shown or hidden.

###### *Type*

Boolean

###### *Options*

* true  
* false (default)

###### *Constraint*

If the badge property is true the chevron property can not be true as well.

---

##### expandable

With the expandable property the chevron on the navigation item can be shown or hidden and that item is required to have children. 

###### *Type*

Boolean

###### *Options*

* true  
* false (default)

###### *Constraint*

If the expandable property is set to true the navigation needs to contain children.   
If the expandable property is set to true the badge property can not be true as well.   
If the expandable property is set to true the item can not have a target.

##### children

With the children property the children of a navigation item can be set to enable expandable navigation items.

###### *Type*

Children

###### *Constraint*

Navigation items can only contain themselves as children. If a navigation is already a child it can not contain children itself. A navigation item can only contain children if chevron is also set to true.

##### is-expanded

With this property the navigation item can be expanded and collapsed.

###### *Type*

Boolean

###### *Options*

* true  
* false (default)

###### *Constraint*

The Is-expanded property can only be true if the expandable property is true.

#### context switcher

##### current-context

The current-context property sets the currently selected context of the context switcher. The title of the current context also sets the currently active context text in the dropdown field of the context switcher.

###### *Type*

Single select

###### *Options*

All currently available contexts.

---

##### is-open

The is-open property controls whether the dropdown is open or not.

###### *Type* 

Boolean

###### *Options*

* true  
* false (default)

---

##### contexts

With the context property the source of the switcher items can be set.

###### *Type*

List(context-switcher-items)

###### *Constraint*

The contexts property can only accept context switcher items. 

#### context switcher items

##### context-name

The context-name sets the name of the context the context switcher item contains.

###### *Type*

Text

---

##### context-description

The context-description sets the description of the context the context switcher item contains.

###### *Type*

Text

---

##### badge

The badge property controls whether the badge of the context switcher item is hidden or not.

###### *Type*

Boolean

###### *Options*

* true  
* false (default)

|  ![][image22] | Overflowing should never happen  and the designer should make sure to choose labels that will not overflow. Still if it ever happens, this is what the overflow would look like. # **Accessibility**

#### Alternative text

The logo and all icons without labels are required to have alternative text to provide meaningful context to screen readers

#### Meaningful link text

It's imperative for designers to select labels for navigation items that are both descriptive and intuitive. This ensures that users, particularly those using assistive technologies, can understand the purpose of each link without needing additional context.

#### Reduced motion

For users with a preference for reduced motion, all animations within the side navigation should be disabled. This ensures a more comfortable experience for individuals sensitive to motion.

#### Focus order

The tabbing order or focus order should follow a coherent sequence. Here is the recommended order:

* Logo  
* Expand/collapse button  
* Navigation content (following a top-to-bottom order for all interactive elements)  
* Footer content (also in a top-to-bottom sequence for all interactive elements)

#### Keyboard support

##### Primary Navigation

When the expand/collapse button has focus pressing the 'Enter' key should toggle the expansion or collapse of the primary navigation.

Pressing the 'Ctrl \+ E' key should also serve the same function of expanding or collapsing the navigation.

##### Navigation Items

###### *For standard navigation items:*

When in focus, pressing 'Enter' should redirect the user to the destination specified by that navigation item.

###### *For expandable navigation items*

When in focus, pressing 'Enter' should toggle the expansion or collapse of that specific navigation item.

If an expandable navigation item was expanded with the keyboard the first item of the children is focused.

#### Screen reader

* Use `aria-label` to provide a name “Main navigation” for the navigation.   
* Logo: If the logo text is an SVG and therefore can not be read by a screen reader alternative text with the same text as the one that can be read visually should be set.  
* Collapse/expand icon: reads the opposite to the current status of the icon. For example, if the navigation is expanded, it reads “Collapse navigation”.   
* Groups: a group is announced by saying “start of navigation section”  
  * Group headings: read as “Group heading:” followed by the group heading  
  * End of group: at the end of a group section, it reads “end of group”  
* Expandable navigation item:  
  * Make sure to use `aria-expanded` to indicate the current state (true or false).  
* Current page indicator:  
  * Use `aria-current="page"` to indicate which navigation link corresponds to the current page or view.  
* Footer items: the footer will be read as any other navigation group.  
* Skip to main content  
  * When using the side navigation make sure to have a “Skip to main content” link at the top of the page to allow screen reader users to bypass the navigation and go straight to the main content if they wish.
